tagline: Leading offshore drilling contractor providing mobile offshore drilling units for global oil and gas exploration and production
hero_kpi_rationale: Fleet size and specification are key competitive levers in the offshore drilling sector. With 36 units (25 floaters and 11 jackups), Noble operates a world-class fleet that determines its ability to win contracts in ultra-deep and highly demanding environments.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated from the leasing and operation of offshore drilling rigs
kpis.description: Revenue is primarily derived from day-rate contracts with oil companies. It is highly dependent on oil prices and offshore exploration activity.
kpis.signal: Revenue of $3.3 billion in 2025, supported by strong demand in offshore drilling

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Profit after all operating expenses, depreciation, and taxes
kpis.description: Net income reflects the company's overall performance after operating costs, depreciation, and taxes.
kpis.signal: Net income of $216.7 million in 2025, or $1.35 per diluted share

kpis.name: Operating Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Cash generated from core offshore drilling operations
kpis.description: Demonstrates the company's ability to generate cash from its drilling contracts, essential for funding maintenance costs and capital investments.
kpis.signal: High operating cash flow of $951.7 million in 2025

kpis.name: Fleet Size
kpis.explanation: Total number of drilling rigs owned or leased
kpis.description: The fleet includes 25 floating units (drillships and semi-submersibles) and 11 jackups. Fleet size and modernity are key competitive levers in the sector, enabling service in ultra-deep and highly demanding markets.
kpis.signal: Fleet of 36 units as of December 31, 2025, comprising 25 floaters and 11 jackups

kpis.name: Cash Balance
kpis.explanation: Amount of cash held by the company at period-end
kpis.description: Cash provides liquidity for contingencies, funding acquisitions, or investing in fleet modernization. No borrowings were drawn on the revolving credit facility in 2025.
kpis.signal: Cash balance of $471.4 million at year-end 2025

kpis.name: Contract Backlog
kpis.explanation: Estimated future revenues from signed drilling contracts
kpis.description: The backlog includes contracted day-rate revenues signed for future periods through 2031. 57% of available days in 2026 are committed, reflecting sustained demand despite recent cyclical pressures.
kpis.signal: Backlog of $7.0 billion as of December 31, 2025, ensuring revenue visibility

kpis.name: Dayrate Trend
kpis.explanation: Trend in prices charged per day of drilling
kpis.description: Dayrates have risen significantly since 2021 but have moderately declined from their 2023-2024 peaks, reflecting demand pressure and increasing competition, although long-term demand remains favorable.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €7.53 Bn in the latest year

risks.title: Dependence on oil and gas price volatility
risks.score_rationale: This risk is central in the 10-K, mentioned first and repeated multiple times. The language is strong ("material adverse effect") and the context shows persistent price volatility (e.g., 2020 vs 2022). The Macro category is highly weighted as it affects the entire business.

risks.title: Intense competition on pricing and fleet overcapacity
risks.score_rationale: The document describes fierce competition, rig overcapacity, and downward pressure on dayrates. The language is alarming ("substantially lower dayrates", "idle for long periods"). A recurring risk exacerbated by new rigs.

risks.title: Customer contract termination or renegotiation
risks.score_rationale: Several paragraphs detail the risk of termination, force majeure, or non-payment. The language is repetitive and concerned ("material adverse effect"). Less existential than pricing, but highly present in the market cycle.

risks.title: Contracts with high-risk national oil companies
risks.score_rationale: The text highlights increased risks (termination without cause, non-payment, disputes). Language is cautious ("can provide no assurance"). Less frequent than other risks, but high severity when realized.

risks.title: Inability to realize contract backlog
risks.score_rationale: The risk of backlog non-execution is explicitly mentioned, with uncertain assumptions on dayrates. Language expresses doubt ("we can provide no assurance"). Direct impact on future revenues.

risks.title: Increased exposure to environmental liabilities
risks.score_rationale: The text mentions limited indemnification clauses and risks of unlimited liability in case of gross negligence. The environmental regulatory framework is tightening, increasing legal risk.

risks.title: Dependence on a few customers and geographic regions
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned but partially cut in the excerpt. Standard language on customer concentration. Less developed than others, but plausible in a niche sector.

ai_positioning.summary: Company NE does not mention artificial intelligence in its annual report.
